clue.text: Remark that's revealing a sinful pride of a sort

indicators.note: something of a sort is a loose version of itself, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comment exposing someone's wicked arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a sort' rearranges A SINFUL PRIDE into the twelve letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip of the tongue held to betray a hidden wish, in Freud's theory, is a remark that reveals more than intended.

clue.text: Discontented, like Casca with his rent?

definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Antony shows the gash in Caesar's cloak 'the ... Casca made'

explanation.walkthrough: The 'rent' is not money but a tear: Antony's speech over Caesar's body names the hole made by the dagger of the envious Casca.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealous resentment of another's good fortune is a kind of discontent.

clue.text: Risks being left out of areas of the church

indicators.note: something taken out of a word is removed from its letters here

parts.note: chancels are the parts of a church around the altar

explanation.surface: Gambles made when someone is excluded from parts of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes the L from CHANCELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chances, as a verb, means takes risks or gambles on something.

clue.text: Knight wearing showy decoration

indicators.note: a garment wearer is surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: garish means gaudy or showy
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight dressed in flashy ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A garnish is decoration added to food, an ornamental touch.

clue.text: I would back horse — so do this to my savings?

definitions.text: so do this to my savings?

indicators.note: putting something back reverses it, so the contraction is written backwards

parts.note: I would contracts to I'd
a pinto is a piebald horse

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on a horse and wonders whether to raid the nest egg to do it.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw on savings is to dip into them, taking some out.

clue.text: Bluish-green vein, the last for inoculation

parts.note: a lode is a vein of ore

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A medic notes a vein's colour and that it's the final one to use for a jab.
explanation.definitionFit: Loden is a dull green colour, from the waterproof wool cloth of that shade.

clue.text: Have in mind backing instrument: cello certainly contributes

indicators.note: backing here means read in the reverse direction
the words contribute their letters, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: A backing musician says the cello definitely adds to the sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contributes' points to TCELLOCER inside 'instrument: cello certainly', and 'backing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To recollect is to remember, keeping something in mind.

clue.text: Constable may be following conductor carefully

definitions.meaning: a police constable patrolling a round is out on patrol
a musician keeping time with the conductor's beats

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both on a police patrol route and in time with the music's rhythm.

clue.text: Peacock shows mating frenzy, by the way

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
the rut is the season of animal mating

explanation.surface: A bird in display mode beside a road.
explanation.definitionFit: To peacock is to show off, swaggering just as a strut does.

clue.text: How to warm this woman up?

definitions.text: How to warm this woman up?

parts.words: How to warm this woman up?
parts.note: read as an instruction, a verb for warming followed by a pronoun for the woman spells a girl's name

explanation.walkthrough: The clue's own answer to its question is a three-letter heat verb plus 'her', which together are a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Heather is a woman's given name, and split it is an instruction to warm her.

clue.text: Small discount is not very polite

definitions.meaning: a little taken off the price
rather rude or out of order

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a little reduction and slightly unacceptable behaviour.

clue.text: Made part of a pair, preserved with taking of wife

indicators.note: one word taking another takes it inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: tinned food is preserved in cans

explanation.surface: A canned food is paired off when the wife is included.
explanation.definitionFit: To be twinned is to be paired with another, matched as one of two.

clue.text: Holiday destination: Kent, perhaps, excepted

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England, abbreviated SE
aside, as in 'aside from', means excepted

explanation.surface: A resort is recommended, with one English county left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in the south-east corner of England, famous for its coastal resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: The coast is a classic place to go on a holiday trip.

clue.text: The Derbyshire custom to treat red swellings

indicators.note: treating something processes it, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A local ritual is a remedy for inflamed lumps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to treat' rearranges RED SWELLINGS. Derbyshire is an English county where villages decorate their wells with flower pictures each summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The decorating of springs with flower panels is a traditional Derbyshire summer custom.

clue.text: G-man going about always flushed

indicators.note: a piece going about another surrounds it

parts.note: a G-man is an FBI agent, a fed
ever means always

explanation.surface: An FBI agent on his rounds is permanently red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish and fevered both describe a flushed, hot state.

clue.text: For example, fear European travel

parts.note: motion is movement or travel

explanation.surface: A traveller in Europe admits being afraid of journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: Fear is one example of a feeling.

clue.text: Carry out duke — His Grace is in a bad way

indicators.note: something in a bad way is in disorder, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A duke is carried out while a dignitary is in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a bad way' rearranges HIS GRACE into ISCHARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a duty is to carry it out or perform it.

clue.text: Made 3 runs in excellent start for Durham

indicators.note: the runs letter is placed in the word for excellent

parts.note: ace means excellent
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A cricketer scored three runs in a fine opening for Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to 3-down, a discharge: a current that jumps a gap is said to arc. Durham is an English county cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric spark jumping a gap arcs, so made a discharge means arced.

clue.text: It may cut the top of head — well, not the sides

parts.note: the scalp is the skin on top of the head

indicators.note: dropping a word's sides leaves its middle letters

explanation.surface: Something might slice the crown, but not the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the sides' leaves EL from WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's small blade is a cutting instrument.

clue.text: Popular taste for example said to be a contributor to some services

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: said means what follows is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: taste is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: A popular sense, it is claimed, plays a part in church worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt aromatic resin is used in some religious ceremonies.

clue.text: With this overhead, could one maintain a lot of liquidity?

definitions.text: With this overhead, could one maintain a lot of liquidity?

parts.words: With this overhead, could one maintain a lot of liquidity?
parts.note: overhead suggests business costs and liquidity cash, but read literally it is a big hat that might hold plenty of fluid

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about company finance; read literally, it is a cowboy's large hat that might hold a great volume of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall wide cowboy hat is named for its supposed capacity to hold a lot of liquid.

clue.text: Needing more help, being overweight, to get back into skimpy clothes provided

indicators.note: the reversed piece goes into the gap between the other pieces

parts.note: shorts are skimpy legwear
fed means supplied or provided

indicators.note: the word is turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: fat means overweight

explanation.surface: Someone heavy struggles to fit back into brief clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the overweight word and 'into' places it in the gap between the clothes and the provided piece; 'being' and 'to get' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A business without enough workers needs more help.

clue.text: Release heretic relative

parts.note: the Cathars were a medieval heretical sect
sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: Freeing a heretical family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is the emotional release of pent-up feelings.

clue.text: Having source of milk, I'm beginning to eat, now?

parts.note: a teat is a nipple, a source of milk
taken as written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A baby wonders whether it's time to feed.
explanation.definitionFit: The question 'now?' is asked when it is the hour for the afternoon meal.

clue.text: The loan is free? That's intoxicating

indicators.note: letters set free from their order can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to hear a loan costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethanol is the alcohol in drinks, the substance that makes people drunk.

clue.text: Hunter's guide, remarkably rakish one

indicators.note: remarkably suggests something altered, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A guide for a hunter is strikingly dashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A shikari is a big-game hunter or hunting guide in India.

clue.text: Cheering also up in the circle

indicators.note: the reversed piece is placed in the circle word

parts.note: a ring is a circle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read upward, so reversed

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: Fans also cheering from the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' suits a down clue, where the word for also is read from bottom to top before 'in' sets it within the circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Rooting for a team means cheering it on, in American usage.

clue.text: Additional statement American author pronounced?

indicators.note: pronounced means the word is spoken, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: an author is a writer, which in an American accent is said with a soft middle consonant

explanation.surface: Asking how an American novelist's name is said.
explanation.walkthrough: In American speech the T in the middle of the author word softens towards a D.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a clause added to a document or statement.
